article.title: NFL EDGE Monday Morning Brief
article.dek: Week 9 is one game from done — the Bears survived a wild Sunday night — and tonight's Bills-Vikings game is the only price left.

items.headline: Lead: the Bears survived five turnovers and won at the buzzer — one game left in Week 9
paragraphs: The Bears beat the Buccaneers 27-24 on Sunday night. Cairo Santos kicked a 38-yard field goal as time expired. Caleb Williams threw four interceptions — the first four-pick game of his career — but hit Colston Loveland for 38 yards on the final drive to set up the winner.

Tampa Bay forced five turnovers and still lost. Bucky Irving scored twice and Baker Mayfield tied the game at 24 with a two-point conversion and 2:51 left. Chicago is 7-2 with four straight wins. Tampa Bay falls to 3-6. Both teams go on bye now and play again November 22.
One game is left in Week 9. The Bills visit the Vikings tonight at 8:15 p.m. ET at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis. Both teams are 6-1.
items.takeaway: Bears 27, Buccaneers 24 — Santos won it at the buzzer — and only Bills at Vikings is left tonight, 8:15 p.m. ET, both teams 6-1.

items.headline: Injuries: Pickens sat, Ferguson gets more tests today, and Wentz starts for Minnesota tonight
paragraphs: Cowboys receiver George Pickens sat out Sunday against the Colts with a hamstring injury. It was his first missed game since joining Dallas. Coach Brian Schottenheimer said Pickens will work through the whole week again, and his chances of playing against the 49ers on November 15 are good if he has no setbacks.

Cowboys tight end Jake Ferguson caught a touchdown, then left in the third quarter with a stinger and a left knee injury. He did not return. Schottenheimer said Ferguson gets more imaging on his knee today. Safety P.J. Locke suffered his second concussion in as many weeks.
For tonight: Carson Wentz starts at quarterback for Minnesota. Inactives come out about 90 minutes before kickoff, so the final names for Bills-Vikings are not out yet this morning.
items.takeaway: Pickens sat with a hamstring injury; Ferguson left with a knee injury and gets more tests today; Wentz starts for Minnesota tonight.

items.headline: Weather: tonight is indoors, so weather is a non-factor
paragraphs: Bills-Vikings is at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, which has a roof. No wind, no rain, no cold to adjust for. Weather does not change anything about tonight's game.
items.takeaway: Tonight is indoors in Minneapolis — weather is a non-factor.

items.headline: The board still has not flipped — last week's cards are still showing, so tonight goes through Check
paragraphs: The app board still shows Week 8. It was generated November 2 and has not flipped to Week 9, let alone Week 10. The headline cards on it are from last Monday night's Bears-Seahawks game: Hit Rate on the Seahawks moneyline at -175, Balanced and Value both on the Bears +3 at -102. Those games are done. Do not bet those cards.

Here is how to read them anyway, because the same three cards will be back when the board flips. Hit Rate is the pick most likely to win — the Seahawks moneyline, with the model at 56.1% against a market price that needed 60.4%. It forgoes value for win probability, and the app's own tutorial says Hit Rate is not Profit Rate. Balanced is the middle ground, a strong pick without paying too much. Value is always the model's plus-EV play — the Bears +3, with the model at 50.6% against a market that needed 50.5%, for a small positive edge.

For tonight, there is no card to read, so use Check. Tap Check, type in your book's line and price for Bills-Vikings, and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator and returns a bet or no-bet verdict on your price. That is a full re-evaluation, not a blind override. Monday game? Monday check.
items.takeaway: The board still shows last week's Week 8 cards, so tonight's Bills-Vikings price goes through Check — type in your book's line and price and let the app give you a verdict on it.

items.headline: Learn the Game: closing line value — did you beat the market?
paragraphs: Closing line value, or CLV, is a simple idea. It asks whether the price you took was better than the price the game closed at. If you bet a team at +3.5 and the line closed at +2.5, you got a better number than the final market. If you bet at -3 and it closed at -3.5, you got a worse one.

Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: say you take a team at +3 at -110 on Tuesday. By Sunday the same bet is +2.5 at -110. You beat the closing line by half a point. That does not mean your bet wins — the team can still lose. It means you bought at a better price than the market settled on, and over a lot of bets, buying better prices is how an edge shows up.

The flip side matters too. If your number keeps closing worse than the price you took, your timing is costing you, even when individual bets win. Check the closing line after the game, not just the final score.
items.takeaway: Closing line value asks whether your price was better than the closing price — beating the close does not guarantee a win, but buying better prices over time is how an edge shows up.

items.headline: The Monday total fell four points this week, and the Bears won but did not cover
paragraphs: Bills-Vikings opened with Buffalo as a 2.5-point favorite and a total of 47.5. This morning the Bills are -3 at DraftKings and FanDuel, -3.5 at some books, and the total is 43.5 at DraftKings and FanDuel, 44 to 44.5 elsewhere. The spread moved a point toward Buffalo. The total fell four points.

Sunday night moved too. The Bears closed as 6-point favorites after opening the week at -3.5, and the total closed at 47.5. The final was 27-24 — 51 points. The favorite won but did not cover. The total went over.

The app board has caught none of this. It still shows Week 8 prices from November 2. If your book's number for tonight looks different from the ones above, run it through Check and let the app judge your price, not last week's.
items.takeaway: Bills opened -2.5 with a 47.5 total; now -3 and 43.5. The Bears closed -6, won 27-24, and did not cover.

items.headline: One game left — if Check says bet on your number, bet it now
paragraphs: There is one price left this week. If you like a side or a total tonight, run your book's exact price through Check. If it says bet, bet the good number now — a good number today beats a hoped-for number later, because waiting lets the number drift the wrong way too. Wait only if your bet depends on an inactive-list name, and those come out about 90 minutes before kickoff.
One more thing: settlement is manual, and the tracker only works if you are honest with yourself. Log the losers too.
items.takeaway: Run tonight's price through Check — if it says bet, bet the good number now; wait only if your bet depends on an inactive-list name. And log the losers too.
